deploy.//: Migrations run before the app starts. Without this, a schema change deployed fine and then failed at runtime on the missing column — production sat three migrations behind for days, which broke login and left Accruals with no tables. `prisma` is a runtime dependency so the binary survives the production install, and it is invoked directly rather than through npx so boot never reaches for the registry. `migrate deploy` only applies committed migrations and is a no-op when there are none, so the trade-off is deliberate: a migration that cannot apply now blocks the release instead of shipping a build that cannot serve requests.
deploy.//healthcheck: Deliberately absent. The healthcheck was failing every attempt with `service unavailable` while the container logged nothing, which blocked all releases and gave no diagnosis in return — Railway rolls the deploy back before the logs are worth reading. Without `healthcheckPath` the deploy goes live as soon as the container starts, so the app's real behaviour can be observed directly against the public URL. Note the trade-off: nothing now verifies that the app serves traffic before it replaces the running version, so a broken release will go live returning 502s instead of being held back. Restore by re-adding `"healthcheckPath": "/api"` with a `healthcheckTimeout` of at least 300 — the window has to cover `migrate deploy` too, since migrations run in the start command above, and 60s was not enough.
